# Jubilees Chapter 10 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 10:3 — Noah's prayer: "God of the spirits of all flesh"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "God of the spirits of all flesh" | Literal Ge'ez divine address |
| LOGOS | "God of the spirits of all flesh" | Same — strong agreement |
| PNEUMA | "God who governs every living spirit" | Paraphrases the divine title |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET (identical). "God of the spirits of all flesh" is a formulaic divine address with biblical parallels (Num 16:22; 27:16); it should be preserved as such.

---

## 10:8 — Mastema's petition: "power of my will" vs. "my function"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I shall not be able to execute the power of my will on the sons of men" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "I will be unable to execute my power of will over the sons of men" | Formal, same content |
| PNEUMA | "I won't be able to exercise my function over human beings" | "Function" replaces "power of will" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Power of will" is the Jubilees technical concept — Mastema's delegated authority to test and tempt. "Function" (PNEUMA) is too bureaucratic and loses the adversarial charge.

---

## 10:11 — "subject before Satan on the earth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "that they might be subject before Satan on the earth" | Preserves "Satan" as the name given here |
| LOGOS | "to be subject before Satan on the earth" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "to answer to Satan on earth" | "Answer to" is colloquial |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Subject before Satan" is the formal subjugation formula. The use of "Satan" alongside "Mastema" in this passage (Mastema = v.8, Satan = v.11) shows the two names are interchangeable here.

---

## 10:12 — Noah's book: "medicines of their diseases" vs. "remedies"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all the medicines of their diseases, together with their seductions" | "Medicines" and "seductions" |
| LOGOS | "all the remedies for their diseases, together with their enticements" | "Remedies" and "enticements" |
| PNEUMA | "every remedy...and all the ways the demons seduce people" | "Seduce" for "enticements" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Remedies" is more natural than "medicines" in this context (the book covers counter-measures, not pharmaceuticals per se). "Enticements" captures the sense better than PNEUMA's "seduce" which has a sexual connotation.

---

## 10:19 — Mastema instigates the Tower

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the prince of Mastema desired to accomplish all this" | "Prince of Mastema" — possessive |
| LOGOS | "The prince Mastema desired to accomplish all of this" | "Prince Mastema" — appositional |
| PNEUMA | "It was Mastema who pushed this whole project forward" | Colloquial, drops "prince" |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "The prince Mastema" preserves Mastema's title. "Prince" = Ge'ez sar, a title for a ruling spirit. PNEUMA's colloquial phrasing drops an important honorific.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
